definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Coordination Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified frame that binds one Product, an optional Project, an optional Goal, a stable purpose, intended consumers and uses, subject scope, source policies, and zero or more references to independently owned Bounded Contexts. A material change to Product, Project, Goal, or purpose requires a successor identity.
definition.formal_model: CoordinationContext = (id, product_ref, project_ref?, goal_ref?, purpose, consumer_refs, intended_uses, subject_scope, source_policy_refs, bounded_context_refs, owner_ref, lifecycle, revision_history, challenge_route); |product_ref|=1; |project_ref|<=1; |goal_ref|<=1; material_anchor_change => successor_required.
definition.operational_interpretation: Use a Coordination Context to frame why selected information is needed and by whom. Resolve changing source selections into separate views rather than mutating the context identity.
definition.plain_language_voice: The durable frame that says what a piece of work is about, why information is needed, and who will use it.
definition.domain_context_voice: In CyberAlchemy Lab, Coordination Context records belong under coordination/contexts and may reference Governance or Ontology Lifecycle bounded contexts without becoming either one.
definition.boundary: A Coordination Context is not a DDD Bounded Context, Product, Project, Goal, session, prompt, source selection, resolved view, authority envelope, decision, or execution permission.

promotion_blockers: CAV2-D66 selector admission for this exact specialization is absent.
The Coordination Context owner role and artifact type are not admitted.

definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Bounded Context is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic boundary inside which one declared domain model and one Ubiquitous Language are intended to remain internally consistent for an explicit scope and set of exclusions. Its relationships to other Bounded Contexts exist only through separately owned directional Context Maps and contracts.
definition.formal_model: BoundedContext = (id, version, domain_model_ref, ubiquitous_language_ref, scope, exclusions, semantic_owner_ref, contract_refs, context_map_refs, lifecycle, evidence_refs, challenge_route); unique(id,version); every cross_context_dependency => exists exact directional ContextMap.
definition.operational_interpretation: Create a Bounded Context only after naming its model, language, owner, scope, exclusions, and cross-context dependencies. Reject context identity inferred from a package name or directory.
definition.plain_language_voice: A named boundary within which words and domain rules have one deliberately consistent meaning.
definition.domain_context_voice: CyberAlchemy Lab treats Governance and Ontology Lifecycle as distinct bounded-context candidates because authority decisions and ontology event history have related but non-identical models and owners.
definition.boundary: A Bounded Context is not a folder, module, package, Product, capability, Coordination Context, Project, Goal, team, deployment unit, database, or authority grant.

promotion_blockers: No admitted Lab source provides a canonical Bounded Context meaning.
The proposed meaning requires definition-owner and bounded-context-owner review.

definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Ubiquitous Language is the owner-governed set of expressions, concepts, relations, interpretation rules, usage surfaces, ambiguities, and revision routes used to express one Bounded Context's model. Each load-bearing expression resolves to one current concept disposition within that context or remains explicitly unresolved.
definition.formal_model: UbiquitousLanguage = (id, bounded_context_ref, concept_refs, expression_bindings, relation_bindings, interpretation_rules, usage_surfaces, owner_refs, ambiguity_records, revision_state); each current binding belongs_to(bounded_context_ref); shared_spelling =/=> shared_meaning.
definition.operational_interpretation: Use the same owned expressions across relevant conversation, model, specification, implementation, and evidence surfaces inside the context; record ambiguities and bridges instead of forcing equivalence.
definition.plain_language_voice: The shared vocabulary used to discuss and build one bounded part of the domain.
definition.domain_context_voice: Governance and Ontology Lifecycle must each own their language. Terms such as decision, event, lifecycle, and state cross the boundary only through explicit mappings.
definition.boundary: A Ubiquitous Language is not a repository-wide dictionary, canonical definition registry, glossary file, ontology, programming language, maintenance discipline, or proof that every participant understands the same thing.

promotion_blockers: The source Language and Ubiquitous Language meanings are package-local candidates.
No external DDD source has been admitted for the established term.

definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Context Map is a versioned, owner-approved set of typed directional relationships between exact Bounded Context versions. Each relationship declares upstream and downstream roles, integration or translation contracts, information and authority limits, owners, evidence, drift handling, and change coordination.
definition.formal_model: ContextMap = (id, version, context_refs, relationships, owner_refs, lifecycle, evidence_refs, drift_route); Relationship = (source_context_version, target_context_version, direction, relationship_kind, contract_refs, translation_refs, information_boundary, authority_boundary, owners); directory_or_import_proximity =/=> relationship.
definition.operational_interpretation: Use a Context Map before one context consumes another context's language, model, events, or contracts. Fail closed when direction, version, contract, or ownership is missing.
definition.plain_language_voice: The explicit map showing how bounded contexts depend on or translate for one another and who owns each side.
definition.domain_context_voice: The first Lab map will connect Ontology Lifecycle downstream to Governance upstream while leaving the exact DDD relationship pattern for a separate owner decision.
definition.boundary: A Context Map is not a directory tree, dependency scan, import graph, ontology relation set, runtime topology, authority transfer, or evidence that two contexts agree.

promotion_blockers: The exact Governance to Ontology Lifecycle relationship pattern remains unresolved.
Context-map owner roles and artifact type are not admitted.

definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Capability Instance is an owner-local, version-exact realization or specialization of one Product Capability inside an explicitly declared coordination and semantic context. It binds separate parent and instance authority lanes, inherited contract, extension scope, adoption decision, D65 construction stages, conformance evidence, lifecycle, drift and recomposition routes, recursion budget or stop, and terminal handoff.
definition.formal_model: CapabilityInstance = (id, capability_version_ref, coordination_context_ref, bounded_context_refs, parent_authority_claim, instance_authority_claim, inherited_contract_ref, extension_scope, adoption_decision_ref, construction_binding_ref, conformance_refs, lifecycle, drift_route, recomposition_route, recursion_stop, terminal_handoff); instance =/=> parent; conformance =/=> authority.
definition.operational_interpretation: Instantiate a capability only after binding the exact parent version and local owner. Keep authored specification, generated projections, implementation, evidence, residue, and handoff inside the instance envelope.
definition.plain_language_voice: A locally owned realization of a reusable capability, connected to its blueprint without becoming the blueprint.
definition.domain_context_voice: The existing ontology-lifecycle vertical may become a capability instance inside the new Ontology Lifecycle bounded context only after its exact parent capability and complete recursive and construction bindings are selected.
definition.boundary: A Capability Instance is not the Product Capability, Bounded Context, Coordination Context, Project, Goal, directory, implementation component, deployment, conformance result, or authority grant.

promotion_blockers: CAV2-D64 and CAV2-D67 selectors are not admitted for this specialization.
The parent Product Capability for the current ontology-lifecycle vertical is not admitted.

definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Context Migration Manifest is an immutable candidate plan that binds exact source repository selectors and digests to explicit artifact dispositions, proposed destination identities and paths, dependency order, preimages, expected postimages, validation obligations, owner gates, rollback boundaries, exclusions, and unresolved residue for one bounded migration scope.
definition.formal_model: ContextMigrationManifest = (id, source_repository, source_selections, dispositions, destination_candidates, dependency_order, preimages, expected_postimages, validation_obligations, owner_gates, rollback_boundary, exclusions, residue, lifecycle); manifest_exists =/=> source_admitted or migration_authorized or migrated.
definition.operational_interpretation: Create one manifest per context migration epoch. Reject broad directory copies, inferred admissions, untracked splits, or destinations without identity and owner decisions.
definition.plain_language_voice: The exact, reviewable plan for what context material might move, where it would go, what would change, and how to stop or reverse safely.
definition.domain_context_voice: The Ontology Lifecycle manifest will eventually select exact bytes from the current root vertical and external CyberAlchemy-v2 evidence, but this CTX-00 pack does not create that manifest or authorize relocation.
definition.boundary: A Context Migration Manifest is not source admission, execution authorization, a file-copy command, lineage proof, migration receipt, context admission, publication, or deployment.

promotion_blockers: The migration-owner role is not bound.
No selected context postimages or rollback contract exists.

definition.scientific_formal_voice: A Context Lineage Record is an immutable, owner-qualified statement relating exact predecessor and successor context identities through one typed lineage disposition, with source and destination versions, preserved and changed semantic scopes, decision evidence, effective boundary, challenges, and residue. It records identity history without inferring semantic equivalence or admission.
definition.formal_model: ContextLineageRecord = (id, predecessor_context_ref?, successor_context_refs, lineage_kind, source_version, destination_versions, preserved_scope, changed_scope, decision_ref, evidence_refs, effective_boundary, challenge_route, residue); lineage_kind in {preserved, successor, split, merged, superseded, withdrawn}; lineage =/=> equivalence or admission.
definition.operational_interpretation: Write a lineage record after context identity and migration decisions are known. Use it to preserve splits, successors, mergers, supersession, and withdrawal without rewriting predecessor history.
definition.plain_language_voice: The durable record explaining how an old context identity relates to its successors and which meanings stayed the same or changed.
definition.domain_context_voice: Ontology Lifecycle will require lineage from the current unclassified vertical to its future bounded-context package; the record must say that directory continuity alone is not semantic identity continuity.
definition.boundary: A Context Lineage Record is not a migration manifest, source admission, context map, alias, redirect, Git rename, equivalence proof, promotion decision, or permission to delete the predecessor.

promotion_blockers: The lineage-owner role and lineage artifact type are not admitted.
No predecessor and successor context artifacts exist for an exact lineage statement.
